messages:
tara: Quick heads-up: deployed Marabou-int5 (per-channel quant) to staging for a cross-lingual embed QA. Please run language-sliced checks.
vikram: on it. I'll run recall@1/5/10 by language buckets: en, es, pt, ar, zh, hi. dataset=prod-crosslingual-40k. baseline=orca-embed-multilang-v1.
elen: freeze tokenizer v2.0 for parity. include silhouette, topk_entropy, centroid_shift, and mean_cosine_by_lang.
eval-bot: Job 672433 queued by vikram. model=marabou-int5 dataset=prod-crosslingual-40k subsets=en,es,pt,ar,zh,hi metrics=recall@1,5,10;silhouette;topk_entropy;centroid_shift seeds=4
vikram: early scalars: english recall@1 -0.8% abs; spanish -2.2% abs; portuguese -1.9% abs; arabic -5.6% abs; chinese -3.8% abs; hindi -4.9% abs. global -2.4%.
ciara: whoa arabic/hindi/zh hit hard. are these short queries or long?
vikram: split shows short (<8 tokens) and named-entity-heavy queries trending worse in low-resource langs. english long queries ok.
tara: can you dump 10 failing Arabic/Hindi cases with top5 neighbors? want to check tokenization vs semantic swap. try to include transliteration cases.
vikram: sample dump:
```
q (ar): "كيف أغير كلمة المرور"  (#tokens=4)
baseline top1: "خطوات إعادة تعيين كلمة المرور" (cos=0.86)
marabou top1: "استرداد الحساب" (cos=0.78)
marabou top2: "خطوات إعادة تعيين كلمة المرور" (cos=0.76)
```
```
q (hi): "पासवर्ड रीसेट कैसे करें" (#tokens=4)
baseline top1: "पासवर्ड रीसेट निर्देश" (cos=0.88)
marabou top1: "खाता पुनर्प्राप्ति विकल्प" (cos=0.81)
marabou top2: "पासवर्ड रीसेट निर्देश" (cos=0.79)
```
seems like paraphrase swaps and margin compression, not full drift. tokenization may split scripts differently.
elen: interesting: embedding norms by lang: mean L2 for ar/hi/zh down ~6-9% vs baseline, var up. silhouette_ar down -0.04. centroid_shift for short_ar ~0.12 cosine units. that's large.
ciara: could be quantization interacting badly with script-specific subword merges. we tried per-channel quant; maybe per-tensor for embedding projection helps cross-lingual stability.
tara: can we test two mitigation branches: A) per-channel + per-language bias-correction post-quant (apply small additive correction per output dim computed on small lang-heldout) B) keep multihead-proj layers fp16 (selective-fp16) and quant rest to int5. also try temperature scaling on cosine scores for ranking.
vikram: running quick A/B microtests on 10k lang slices. config snippet: ```./eval/run.sh --model marabou-int5 --baseline orca --slices ar,hi,zh --mitigations biascorr_lang,selective_fp16 --seeds 3``` ETA ~12m
eval-bot: Job 672434 queued (lang-microtests).
vikram: quick micro results: biascorr_lang reduces ar recall@1 gap 5.6% -> 1.6% abs; hi 4.9% -> 1.2%; zh 3.8% -> 1.0%. selective-fp16 reduces gaps to <0.8% but latency p50 +9ms. temp-scaling alone reduced topk_entropy but not recall_gap.
ciara: bias-corr looks promising: small perf benefit and much lower latency hit. how about cost delta?
tara: preliminary cost savings still ~18% vs baseline. selective-fp16 cost delta smaller due to fp16 in big layers.
elen: one more check: multilingual retrieval end-to-end (translate queries -> retrieve -> rerank) shows downstream exact-match F1 unchanged in en but improved with bias-corr in low-resource langs. good sign.
vikram: note: tokenizer edgecases: mixed-script queries (latin+arabic) cause outliers; I filtered 42 such cases and global metrics stabilized ~0.2% better. recommend excluding mixed-script edgecases from SLOs or handling them separately.
ciara: ops: add canary fallback to orca-embed when per-lang recall@1 drop >2.0% for any language over 5m window. also add alert for centroid_shift >0.08 in short bucket.
ops-bot: Canary rule queued: fallback_model=orca-embed trigger_lang_recall1_drop_pct=2.0 per_lang_window_mins=5 centroid_shift_threshold=0.08
tara: action items: 1) vikram run 100k holdouts for biascorr_lang branch + selective-fp16 for comparison; 2) elen compute uMAP deltas and per-lang centroid heatmaps; 3) ciara draft model card note about cross-lingual sensitivity and recommended fallback + tokenization guidance.
vikram: starting holdouts now. will post final numbers and visual diffs when done.
ciara: one more: add a small language-detection step in pipeline to pick fallback early if lang_confidence<0.8; that would mitigate mixed-script noise.
tara: good suggestion, add to ticket. thanks everyone 44d. keeping thread for follow-ups only.
